CyberTrace: DNS Exfiltration Detection

Complete Technical Project, Architecture, Experiment & Verification Report

Repository: vid6848/dns-exfiltration-detection
Evaluation Type: Diagnostic Development Evaluation (Outer Fold 5)
Evaluated Records: 45,240 records (43,340 Benign, 1,900 Attack)
Selected Model Artifact: artifacts/aws_benign_expansion_v0.1/random_forest.joblib
Calibrated Threshold: 0.89 (FPR = 0.00% on Diagnostic Set)
Full Stack Implementation: FastAPI Backend + React 18 / Vite 6 Dashboard

1. Aim and Objectives

The Domain Name System (DNS) is an indispensable protocol for Internet communications, resolving human-readable hostnames to IP addresses. Because recursive resolvers require unhindered egress via UDP and TCP port 53, perimeter network firewalls rarely restrict or deeply inspect DNS traffic. Consequently, adversaries exploit DNS queries as a covert communication channel for DNS Tunneling and Data Exfiltration.

In an exfiltration scenario, malicious software encodes confidential payloads (e.g., credentials, files, or telemetry) into the variable subdomain labels of DNS queries directed toward an adversary-controlled authoritative nameserver (e.g. c2a9f1.0f9hzh.attacker-tunnel.live). Recursive resolvers blindly relay these packets, bypassing egress filters.

Core Project Goals:
  1. Safe & Leakage-Free Preprocessing: Build a deterministic schema normalizer that eliminates target labels, IP identifiers, and raw timestamps from model training inputs.
  2. Rigorous Feature Engineering: Implement exactly 7 structural per-query features and 3 sliding-window behavioral features based on domain length, entropy, and temporal repetition.
  3. Empirical Detection Comparison: Benchmark a frozen 4-indicator statistical baseline rule against an ensemble Random Forest classifier using domain-disjoint cross-validation.
  4. Generalization Diagnosis: Diagnose and resolve enterprise false positives caused by complex benign cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS EC2 subdomains).
  5. Production Full-Stack Serving: Expose real-time inference via an asynchronous FastAPI backend and an interactive React dashboard with automated regression test suites.

2. Environment and Setup

The project is implemented in a cross-platform Python and Node.js environment with minimal third-party dependencies to ensure high execution speed and reproducibility:

  • Core Runtime: Python 3.10+ (tested on Python 3.14 on Windows/Linux) and Node.js 18+ (npm 10+).
  • Backend & ML Libraries: FastAPI (0.115+), Uvicorn (0.34+), Scikit-learn (1.5+), Joblib (1.4+), Pydantic (2.10+), Pytest (8.3+).
  • Frontend Stack: React 18 (18.3.1), Vite (6.0.1), custom Vanilla CSS (design tokens, responsive dark-accent cards).
  • Repository Layout: api/ (REST endpoints), src/preprocessing/ (parsing & schema), src/features/ (lexical & behavioral extractors), src/baseline/ (statistical detector), src/ml/ (training & model bundles), frontend/ (React UI), evaluation/ (metrics & plots), tests/ (automated test suite).

4. Dataset Preparation and Preprocessing Pipeline

A primary failure mode in network intrusion detection research is synthetic dataset leakage and class representation bias. The CyberTrace pipeline established a strict multi-stage ingestion and validation workflow:

4.1 Data Sources & Synthesis

  • Mendeley DNS Exfiltration Capture (Raw Benign): Ingested from data/raw/dataset_dns_exfiltration.csv, comprising 109,359 captured queries from enterprise network environments.
  • Param's Synthetic Attack Generation (10,000 Queries): Generated via data/generate_synthetic_exfiltration.py using verified exfiltration patterns:
    • Encoding schemes: Base32, Base64, and hexadecimal chunks reflecting tools such as iodine and dnscat2.
    • Subdomain chunking: Variable label lengths (15 to 45 characters) concatenated across 3 to 7 labels.
    • Temporal pacing: Fast burst exfiltration (multiple queries/sec) and stealthy slow-drip pacing (randomized 5–60s delays).
  • Public Benign PCAP Expansion (85,604 Queries): Extracted from publisher-labeled university campus traffic (scripts/import_public_benign.py) to expose the model to diverse cloud infrastructure patterns.

4.2 Verified Dataset Populations

Dataset File Total Records Benign Count Attack Count Role in Pipeline

4.3 Normalization & Leakage Elimination

Implemented in src/preprocessing/pipeline.py and verified by verify_ml_feature_safety():

  1. Stripping Target Labels & Identifiers: Ground-truth binary labels, source IPs, destination IPs, and database row IDs are strictly excluded from the feature matrix X.
  2. FQDN Normalization: Strips trailing root dots, lowercases characters, and segments domains into apex domain and subdomains using Public Suffix List rules.
  3. Temporal Separation: Timestamps are used solely for sliding-window delta calculations (Δt) and are never fed directly as numerical features.

5. Feature Engineering Contract

The system enforces an exact, ordered ten-feature contract (FEATURE_ORDER in src/ml/features.py). All features are strictly deterministic and numerical:

Feature Name Category Importance Mathematical Formula & Security Rationale
entropy Lexical (FQDN) 38.99% Shannon entropy over full query: H = -Σ (p_i × log2(p_i)).
Exfiltration encodings (Base64/hex) exhibit high entropy (> 4.0), while benign domains average < 3.2.
subdomain_length Lexical 17.84% Total character count of all prepended subdomain labels.
Tunnels maximize payload capacity per query (often > 35 characters).
query_length Lexical 14.85% Total length of the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) string (capped at RFC 1035 limit of 253 octets).
digit_ratio Lexical 9.54% Ratio of numeric characters: count(digits) / query_length.
Base32 and hexadecimal exfiltration streams sharply elevate numeric density.
longest_label_length Lexical 8.79% Length of the longest dot-separated label. Tunnels pack up to 63 bytes per DNS label.
special_char_ratio Lexical 6.13% Proportion of non-alphanumeric characters: count(non-alphanumeric) / query_length (e.g., dots, hyphens, underscores).
time_interval Behavioral 1.46% Elapsed time in seconds since the previous query from the same (src_ip, apex_domain). Set to -1.0 for initial queries.
number_of_labels Lexical 1.20% Count of dot-delimited segments in the domain name. Multi-stage chunking increases label count.
unique_subdomains Behavioral 0.74% Distinct subdomains requested under the same (src_ip, apex_domain) within a 60.0-second sliding temporal window.
query_frequency Behavioral 0.46% Total number of DNS requests sent by the client to the same apex domain within the 60.0-second sliding window.
Behavioral Sliding Window Implementation (src/features/behavioral.py):
Calculated incrementally across incoming queries using an inclusive window: t in [t_current - 60.0, t_current]. Query history is tracked per (src_ip, apex_domain) pair. IP addresses and raw timestamps are strictly discarded once window grouping is established.

6. Detection Models: Statistical Baseline vs. Random Forest

6.1 Statistical Threshold Baseline (Rudraksh)

The baseline detector (src/baseline/detector.py) provides an explainable, non-ML reference standard using four corroborated indicator thresholds frozen from engineering handoff: 

# Frozen Baseline Threshold Rules (src/baseline/detector.py)
query_length >= 52.0
entropy >= 4.309101
query_frequency >= 41.0
unique_subdomains >= 41.0
Condition: Flagged as SUSPICIOUS if at least TWO indicators cross threshold simultaneously.

By requiring corroborated flags (≥ 2), the baseline avoids triggering on isolated spikes in query length. However, it cannot learn non-linear boundaries between complex features.

6.2 Random Forest Classifier Architecture (Jaynish)

The production classifier is an ensemble Random Forest (src/ml/train.py) designed for robustness and low latency:

  • Hyperparameters: 150 decision trees, max_depth=12, min_samples_leaf=5, max_features="sqrt", class_weight=None, random seed 42.
  • Domain-Disjoint Group K-Fold Splitting: Data is split strictly by apex_domain. All queries belonging to an apex domain reside exclusively within train, validation, or test. This prevents the model from memorizing known domains.
  • Calibrated Decision Threshold (τ = 0.89): Instead of an arbitrary 0.5 threshold, the operating threshold was calibrated against development partitions to enforce pooled FPR ≤ 1.0% and cloud domain FPR ≤ 5.0%.
  • Deterministic Inference: Training uses multi-threaded parallel fitting, but artifact inference locks n_jobs=1 to ensure bit-for-bit reproducible probability sums across platforms.

6.3 Reproducible Training and Evaluation Commands

# Run domain-disjoint group cross-validation training:
python -m src.ml.train --dataset data/processed/cleaned_unified_v0.1.csv

# Execute empirical evaluation comparing Baseline vs Random Forest:
python scripts/evaluate_baseline_vs_rf.py

7.1 Diagnostic Development Evaluation Results (45,240 Records)

Both detectors were evaluated on the exact 45,240 diagnostic records in evaluation/results/baseline_vs_rf_v1/baseline_vs_rf_metrics.json (comprising 43,340 benign records and 1,900 simulated attacks):

Performance Metric Statistical Baseline Random Forest (τ = 0.89) Operational Comparison
Accuracy 97.18% 99.60% +2.42% overall accuracy improvement.
Precision 72.72% 100.00% Zero false alarms on diagnostic set.
Recall (Sensitivity) 52.47% 90.53% +38.06% increase in detected attack queries.
F1-Score 0.6096 (60.96%) 0.9503 (95.03%) Near-optimal harmonic mean.
False Positive Rate (FPR) 0.8629% (374 false alarms) 0.0000% (0 false alarms) Complete elimination of false alarms on evaluated records.
True Positives (TP) 997 / 1,900 1,720 / 1,900 Detected 723 additional exfiltration queries.
False Negatives (FN) 903 / 1,900 180 / 1,900 Reduced missed attacks from 903 to 180.
ROC-AUC / Avg Precision N/A (Rule-based) 0.9978 / 0.9879 Exceptional ranking separation across threshold spectrum.
Inference Latency 12.4 μs / query 45.7 μs / query Processes 21,881 queries/sec on a single CPU core.
Critical Resolution of Conflicting Evaluation Figures:
A prior draft of this report stated an unverified test metric of F1 = 99.98% and FPR = 0.04% on 40,000 queries. Cross-referencing committed project artifacts reveals the actual experimental progression:
  1. Initial Model Failure (v0.1 Holdout): The initial RF model (artifacts/random_forest_v0.1) was tested on 38,155 held-out queries where benign traffic consisted of amazonaws.com. Because AWS EC2 subdomains are long and high in entropy, the initial model produced an FPR of 99.62% (flagging 36,117 benign queries) and an F1 of only 9.52%.
  2. Public Benign Expansion & Calibration: Vidhi expanded benign development data with public PCAP traffic (artifacts/aws_benign_expansion_v0.1) and re-calibrated the threshold to 0.89 to accommodate cloud naming structures.
  3. Verified Diagnostic Result: Evaluated against the 45,240 diagnostic development records (including 36,255 AWS records), the updated model achieved F1 = 95.03% and FPR = 0.00% (1,720 TP, 43,340 TN, 0 FP, 180 FN).
  4. Scientific Scope: These figures are from a diagnostic development evaluation (outer fold 5), not an independent final test on fresh, live production traffic.

8. Backend and Frontend System Architecture

The CyberTrace platform integrates model inference with an asynchronous serving backend and a reactive dashboard client:

8.1 End-to-End Ingestion and Detection Pipeline Flow

Pipeline Lifecycle:
  1. DNS Query Ingestion: The client sends query metadata (timestamp, source IP, destination IP, requested server name) via POST /predict or POST /analyze.
  2. Preprocessing & Normalization: PreprocessingPipeline normalizes the FQDN, extracts the apex domain and subdomain labels, and validates RFC formatting.
  3. Feature Extraction:
    • extract_per_query_features() computes the 7 lexical metrics.
    • BehavioralFeatureExtractor computes the 3 sliding-window metrics using temporal client history.
  4. Model Evaluation: The 10 features are formatted into the canonical feature matrix and evaluated by the Random Forest model bundle.
  5. Decision Thresholding: The calculated probability is compared against τ = 0.89. The endpoint outputs classification verdict (benign vs suspicious), confidence percentage, and inference latency.
  6. User Interface Presentation: The React dashboard displays visual threat banners, color-coded risk bars, and aggregate telemetry.

8.2 API Serving Architecture (Pranay)

  • FastAPI Asynchronous Engine (api/main.py): Loads the model artifact once at startup within an asynchronous lifespan context.
  • CORS Support: Integrated CORSMiddleware allowing local frontend development origins (http://localhost:3000).
  • Batch Behavioral State Accumulation: In POST /analyze, queries are sorted chronologically, processed through a shared sliding-window extractor, and restored to original array index order.

8.3 Security Dashboard Architecture (Bhumit)

  • Modular React Components: Built with clean functional components: Navbar, SingleQueryForm, BatchAnalysisSection, and OfflineEvaluationSection.
  • Live Heartbeat Telemetry: Periodically polls GET /health to display live API connectivity and model status.
  • Zero-Dependency Design System: Custom CSS tokens implementing dark-accent cards, emerald benign pills, red alert banners, and risk progress bars.

12. Scope Limitations, Unimplemented Capabilities & Future Roadmap

In the interest of scientific rigor and operational clarity, the boundaries of the current implementation are explicitly defined:

12.1 Explicit System Limitations

  • Continuous Packet Capture (PCAP Sniffing) Not Implemented: The current system does not include a background packet capture daemon (e.g., using Scapy or libpcap to sniff port 53). Ingestion is currently performed via JSON payloads sent to REST API endpoints.
  • Continuous Live Streaming Alerts Not Implemented: Roadmap endpoints such as /alerts and /statistics for continuous WebSocket push notifications have not been deployed in this release.
  • Plaintext DNS Visibility Prerequisite: The structural feature extractor requires plaintext DNS hostnames. Encrypted DNS protocols (DNS-over-HTTPS / DNS-over-TLS) blind lexical analysis unless decrypted at an enterprise recursive resolver.
  • Diagnostic Development Scope: Reported metrics (95.03% F1, 0.00% FPR) are derived from the 45,240 diagnostic development records. While representative of AWS cloud domains and synthetic attacks, they do not guarantee zero false alarms on unobserved real-world network traffic.

12.2 Future Roadmap

  1. Live Packet Sniffing Daemon: Integrate a modular C++/Python packet sniffer reading raw interface sockets and streaming parsed queries directly to the backend.
  2. Adaptive Thresholding: Implement per-host dynamic thresholds that adjust sensitivity based on the client's baseline query volume.
  3. DoH Handshake Metadata Analysis: Expand detection to Encrypted DNS by analyzing TLS packet sizes, inter-arrival times, and connection burst ratios.
Final Conclusion & System Status:
The CyberTrace DNS Exfiltration Detection system is FULLY FUNCTIONAL, VERIFIED, AND REPRODUCIBLE. The pipeline successfully bridges academic research and practical engineering: from synthetic data generation and leakage elimination to group-disjoint cross-validation, REST API serving, and an intuitive reactive dashboard.
